10 Factors affecting consumption
10.1 Air resistance
The majority of fuel consumed is used to overcome air (wind) resistance that acts against the advancing vehicle.
This means that anything that increases or changes the aerodynamics lines (the design) of a vehicle has a greater impact on consumption.
This is why external accessories, (roof racks, flaps and deflectors, etc.) increase the resistance of the vehicle and, therefore, increase fuel consumption.
It is not advisable to leave the roof rack on the vehicle when it is empty and not being used. It is preferable to carry the load in the boot, whenever possible and not on the roof rack.

5 Generic speed            
           
5.1 Maximum speed limits on interurban roads           
5.1.2 Conventional roads   
Motor vehicles must not exceed the following speed limits:
- Passenger cars, motorbikes, three-wheeled vehicles similar to motorbikes, camper vans with a Maximum Authorised Mass ≤ 3,500 kg and pick-up trucks: 90 km/h.(1)
- Buses, passenger car derivatives and mixed adaptable vehicles: 90 km/h.
- Lorries, trailers, vans, camper vans with a Maximum Authorised Mass > 3,500 kg, articulated vehicles, cars with a trailer and all other vehicles: 80 km/h.  
- Motor tricycles not assimilated to motorcycles and heavy quadricycle: 70 km/h.
(1) On conventional roads with physical separation of the two directions of traffic movement, the road owner may set a speed limit of 100 km/h for passenger cars, motorbikes and camper vans with a Maximum Authorised Mass equal to or less than 3,500 kg.
(Página 173 del manual 'Learning to drive')

FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
 
10.1 Circumstances that cause fatigue
10.1.3 Driver circumstances
Driving for long periods of time without rest breaks or sufficient breaks is the major cause of driver fatigue. Ideally you should plan a journey and include the necessary breaks. Never hurry to reach a destination.
Maintaining a high speed for a long time (requires more concentration).
A change of the driver’ state of health and well being, such as driving when sleepy or fatigued, under the influence of alcohol or when ill.
(Página 37 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Use of the road
 
1 Road positioning
As a general rule, vehicles will drive on the right and as close as possible to the edge of the road, keeping a lateral separation that is large enough to safely pass by other vehicles.
This regulation will be particularly applicable on curves and changes of gradient with reduced visibility. In these cases, even when there is no sign expressly delimiting directions, all drivers must leave the half of the roadway that is for the opposite direction completely free, except when overtaking.
(Página 161 del manual 'Learning to drive')
